name: Graviton Compression Emitter GCE-3 'Flatline'
description:
The GCE-3 generates a focused graviton field projection that temporarily increases the effective gravitational force acting on a target volume by a factor of between 8 and 22 times standard gravity, depending on output setting. The effect is not a beam in the electromagnetic sense — it is a localized distortion of spacetime curvature within a defined area approximately 1.5 meters in diameter at standard operating range. Targets within the field experience sudden, catastrophic increases in effective body weight: at 8G, an unaugmented human experiences immediate skeletal stress fractures and cardiovascular collapse; at 22G, soft tissue rupture is near-instantaneous. The weapon was developed by Ouroboros Energy as a theoretical physics demonstration platform before its military applications became apparent and Arcturus Defense Solutions acquired exclusive licensing rights.

The GCE-3's technological foundation draws on the same graviton manipulation research that underlies GLMZ's commercial anti-gravity transit infrastructure, miniaturized and weaponized in a form that remains deeply controversial among the scientific community. The emitter core contains a crystalline graviton lens array that focuses the field projection with high spatial precision — the 1.5-meter effect radius means trained operators can affect a single target in a crowd without impacting bystanders, though field edge effects at the periphery of the compression zone cause significant discomfort and disorientation in adjacent individuals. The weapon's power requirements are enormous by handheld standards, necessitating a dedicated backpack power unit connected by a reinforced umbilical.

The GCE-3 is one of the most legally contentious weapons in GLMZ. Its use at a labor suppression event in the Palladian Construction sector in 2197 — where seventeen workers were killed and the incident was initially classified as a 'structural collapse' — remains an open wound in the city's political landscape. Ouroboros Energy has faced ongoing regulatory pressure over its foundational research, and the weapon's existence is technically classified at the municipal government level, though this classification is widely understood to be a legal fiction.
specifications: emitter length: 88cm emitter weight: 6.1kg power unit weight: 14.3kg (backpack) umbilical length: 1.2m power source: Ouroboros OE-Heavy cell pack, 9 full-power discharges effect radius at range: 1.5m diameter at 40m effective range: 12–65m (optimal 20–45m) compression range: 8G (incapacitation) to 22G (lethal) field edge effect: Disorientation, nausea, minor skeletal stress in adjacent subjects within 0.5m of field boundary charge time: 3.8 seconds between discharges at full power
tactical_use: GCE-3 deployment is handled by two-person teams: one operator carrying the emitter, one managing the power unit and maintaining umbilical clearance during movement. In military applications, it is used for rapid elimination of high-value hardened targets — individuals in powered armor or with heavy augmentation who are resistant to conventional weapons but whose augments provide no protection against gravitational compression. The weapon's 3.8-second recharge cycle makes it unsuitable for sustained engagements; operators typically fire once per target and reposition. The psychological effect on witnesses is severe and has been deliberately exploited in pacification operations — watching a target collapse under invisible force with no audible discharge is profoundly disorienting.
cultural_context: The GCE-3 is a ghost weapon in GLMZ's cultural consciousness — officially it does not exist, but its effects are known and documented by street communities, labor organizers, and underground journalists who have been tracking its use since 2197. The Palladian Construction massacre has become a reference point for discussions of corporate violence, and the GCE-3 is the weapon that killed those workers, even if no official record admits it. Among military and elite corporate circles, it is spoken of with the particular reverence reserved for weapons that represent genuine technological dominance. Among everyone else, it is a symbol of how far the powerful are willing to go when they believe there will be no consequences.
known_users: Arcturus Defense Solutions special operations units
One confirmed black market unit, current location unknown
story_hooks: The players stumble onto evidence linking the Palladian Construction massacre to a specific GCE-3 serial number — and that unit is currently in the hands of someone who has no idea what they possess or what it connects them to.

Ouroboros Energy's graviton research division has developed a GCE-4 prototype with a 6-meter effect radius and extended range. Someone inside the company wants it destroyed before it can be weaponized. Someone outside the company wants to acquire it for exactly that purpose.

A municipal investigator has been quietly building a case against Arcturus Defense Solutions for the 2197 massacre. She needs a technical expert who can identify GCE-3 wound patterns in autopsy records — and the players are the only people she can trust who have the relevant knowledge and aren't already compromised.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular energy weapon with a distinctly sci-fi aesthetic. The emitter resembles a hybrid between a directed-energy cannon and precision medical equipment—elongated and purposeful, with a tapered muzzle that suggests concentrated field projection rather than ballistic discharge. The design is deliberately clinical, almost surgical in its precision. Paired with its bulky backpack power unit, the complete system reads as a two-person weapons platform despite the compact handheld component.
physical_description.dimensions: Emitter: 88cm length × 12cm width × 8cm height. Muzzle diameter: 4.5cm. Backpack unit: 45cm height × 30cm width × 18cm depth. Umbilical tether: 120cm reinforced polymer conduit.
physical_description.weight_description: The emitter itself (6.1kg) feels balanced and purposeful in trained hands, with weight distributed toward the rear grip. The backpack unit (14.3kg) is heavy and requires proper harness support—designed to be worn by a dedicated operator, not swapped between shooters. The umbilical has noticeable tension and weight.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum alloy frame with reinforced polymer casing. The crystalline graviton lens array is housed in hardened sapphire-composite shrouding. Backpack unit is steel-reinforced composite with heat-dissipation fins.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents around the muzzle and lens housing. The polymer sections show a subtle 'grip-textured' surface treatment. Heat vents along the barrel show oxidation staining consistent with field use. The backpack bears scuff marks and minor cosmetic damage from equipment wear.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Gunmetal gray with charcoal polymer. Accent colors: Brushed titanium around emitter front, deep blue electrical warning stripes on backpack unit. Status indicator lights (dormant state: amber; charging: blue; ready-fire: red) embedded near the grip.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized overmold with micro-texturing for positive grip even with gloved hands. The grip incorporates three finger wells designed for sustained two-handed operation. Slight warmth to the touch due to passive heat bleed from the internal graviton lens.
distinctive_features: Crystalline lens array visible through semi-transparent sapphire composite viewport at muzzle—faintly prismatic, catches light with unusual refractive properties
Charging indicator lights (amber/blue/red) set into grip frame near trigger guard
Reinforced umbilical connection point at emitter rear, sealed with reinforced military-grade connector
Heat vents running along barrel length, showing oxidation and thermal stress patterns
Recessed targeting reticle system on top rail—integrated laser sight housing
Serial number and 'GRAVITON COMPRESSION EMITTER GCE-3' engraved into lower receiver
Backpack unit features external heat-dissipation fins and power status display panel
Danger triangle radiation-style markings and warning text on backpack unit
Umbilical conduit woven with light-reactive fibers for field visibility
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Ironside Armaments logo (stylized iron anvil within a circle) stamped on the lower grip frame. 'GCE-3 FLATLINE' designation in white stencil lettering on backpack unit. Serial plate mounted on rear of emitter, adjacent to umbilical port.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. Heat staining around muzzle from repeated discharge cycles. Minor cosmetic scuffing on polymer casing consistent with equipment transport. No visible damage to critical components. The sapphire lens housing remains pristine—operators understand the cost of replacement. Backpack straps show wear patterns from extended harness use.
